_note: Illustrative example. The library 'tinycsv' and this bug are fictional.

problem.title: Trailing empty field is dropped when a row ends with the delimiter and the file uses CRLF line endings
problem.symptom: Rows ending in ';' return one column fewer than the header. Downstream code fails with 'row has 4 fields, expected 5'.
problem.root_cause:
The 3.1.0 fast path strips '
' with rstrip('
;') instead of rstrip('
'), so a final empty field after the delimiter is removed together with the line ending. LF-only files take a different code path and are unaffected.

reproduction.test_code:
import io
import tinycsv

def test_trailing_empty_field_crlf():
    data = 'a;b;c\r\n1;2;\r\n'
    rows = list(tinycsv.reader(io.StringIO(data, newline=''), delimiter=';'))
    assert rows == [['a', 'b', 'c'], ['1', '2', '']]

fix.description: Strip only the line terminator, never the delimiter. Workaround for users until released: pin tinycsv==3.0.4 or normalize CRLF to LF before parsing.
fix.patch:
--- a/tinycsv/_fast.py
+++ b/tinycsv/_fast.py
@@ -88,7 +88,7 @@ def _split_line(line, delimiter):
-    line = line.rstrip('\r\n' + delimiter)
+    line = line.rstrip('\r\n')
     return line.split(delimiter)
